answer: Each key proves fresh hashrate every epoch: it submits Bitcoin pool shares whose coinbase tag commits to hash(key, epoch nonce), adding up to 200 TH-days of work, about $10 at a hashprice near $0.05 per TH-day. Unlike a walnut shell game, one hidden pea cannot sit under 100 cups: 100 aliases burn about $1,000 per epoch, and every clone adds the same ripple of cost. Renting hashrate is allowed, since the fee is still paid. Check: shares are verified against the header chain, so a reused or stale tag fails and old work is worth no more than marble dust.
